findings.reason: the plan's bounding claim is false at the ingest stage, so its own done-when ("the count of jt-60sa rows outside the three trees whose status changed reads 0"; code chunks only under the four trees) cannot hold unless the prefix scope is applied to those claims or the plan verifies no out-of-scope CodeFile is claimable.
findings.text: §14 runs `discover code jt-60sa --path-prefix … --min-score 0` and states "the seven prefixes already bound the run, so the threshold has nothing left to protect here", but only the file-scan claim is prefix-scoped (`claim_paths_for_file_scan`, imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:99,141); the code-ingest claim at this line matches `CodeFile` facility-wide (`WHERE sf.status='scored' AND sf.score_composite >= $min_score`, no prefix clause), as do `claim_files_for_triage` (imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:279), `claim_files_for_enrichment` (:362), `claim_files_for_scoring` (:446) and `has_pending_code_work` (imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:646, used unpinned at imas_codex/discovery/code/parallel.py:177). With `--min-score` lowered to 0 the run therefore reaches every jt-60sa `CodeFile` at a claimable status facility-wide, not only the seven trees.

findings.reason: widening the shared spec changes every unscoped `--reset-to scanned` invocation facility-wide (a never-scanned `discovered` row would be moved past enumeration), so the plan must name the spec it extends and its bound, or add a dedicated prefix-scoped spec, rather than leave the mechanism to a conditional.
findings.text: §14's root-restore "uses the existing path reset scoped by --root to clear their triage, extending the reset's source statuses only if no existing spec reaches a discovered row with a triage score", but neither `PATH_RESET_SPECS` entry does: `"triaged"` has source_statuses `["scored"]` (imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:255) and `"scanned"` has `["triaged","scored"]` (:262), and the scan claim admits only `discovered` rows whose `triage_composite IS NULL` (imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:488). The plan's conditional therefore fires (the seed overwrite left exactly those three roots at `discovered` with a triage score), and the remedy it implies is adding `discovered` to a shared spec's `source_statuses`.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — §14 adds no new module. It extends two existing owners by one keyword-only parameter each (`reset_to_status(path_prefixes=…)` at imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:63, `create_nodes(create_only=…)` at imas_codex/graph/client.py:611) and adds one shared renderer inside the module that already owns Cypher fragment rendering (imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:268); the complexity stays behind the owners it belongs to.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan's scoped code run is bounded only at the file-scan claim; the four downstream `CodeFile` claims re-implement their predicates without the shared prefix scope, so `--min-score 0` is not confined to the seven `--path-prefix` trees as the plan asserts.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §14 adds no CLI option (`--root`, `--path-prefix`, `--min-score`, `--reset-to` all pre-exist at imas_codex/cli/discover/{paths,code}.py), adds no MCP view or refusal family, and it names what it retires (`seed_missing_roots` retired, `create_child_paths` deleted), so the section accounts for its interface surface.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched the codebase it extends and each cited mechanism verifies: `render_path_prefix_clause` (imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:268) has exactly the eight call sites the plan names (imas_codex/discovery/paths/parallel.py:484,540,597,715,795; imas_codex/discovery/code/graph_ops.py:141,566; imas_codex/discovery/base/reset.py:98), `GraphClient.create_nodes` gained a `create_only` parameter (imas_codex/graph/client.py:611) rather than a parallel writer, the "thirteen ON CREATE SET precedents" claim in frontier.py verifies at 13, and the retired `seed_missing_roots` / `create_child_paths` leave no residue in imas_codex/ or tests/.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — `render_path_prefix_clause` (imas_codex/graph/query_builder.py:268) is a one-line fragment renderer placed in the module that already owns such fragments, replacing eight previously inline spellings; the plan states the reason it exists (one owner for the `any(prefix IN $…)` predicate, so claims and the reset cannot drift), which is the justification the item requires.
